Definition: of uncertain origin; darnel or false grain:--tares.
BiblicalUsage: Zizanion is darnel, the false grain that looks like wheat until the harvest — an enemy sowed it in the field while men slept, and the servants asked whether to pull it up. Jesus said no: let both grow together until the harvest, or the wheat would be rooted up with the tares. The field is the world, the good seed are the children of the kingdom, and the tares are the children of the wicked one.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this parable keeps me from playing judge before the harvest. God sees the difference between wheat and tares even when I cannot, and He will sort them at the end — my work is to grow as wheat, not to tear up the field.
